story.head: The Canadiens are on a heater
paras: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Pittsburgh on Oct 3. The Canadiens have won four straight, while the Pens (5-6-2) lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah on Thursday. Going in, the Penguins are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Canadiens second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.462) says: their chances are worth about .559, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.692) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Penguins get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), so the Canadiens have the edge over them on forecheck pressure. The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd) and take more penalties than they draw (32nd). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th), so the Penguins could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them.

Erik Karlsson (2 G / 11 A / 13 P in 13 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Evgeni Malkin (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 12 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Canadiens, Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Lane Hutson (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) is next in line.
Sergei Murashov (0-3-1 / .883 SV% in 4 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh. Jacob Fowler (6-1-0 / .942 SV% in 7 GS) has been terrific for Montréal and is expected to start.
